full_judgment:
2. The facts involved in the case, in short, arc that the suit land originally belonged to one Jahur Ali who died leaving Mobaswar Ali and Tobarak Ali as sons. Then Tobarak Ali died being bachelor having Mobaswar Ali as his heir and thus, Mobaswar Ali got the entire suit land. Mobaswar Ali while possessing the suit land died leaving Ashob Ali as son and Hazera Bibi as daughter who then sold the suit land measuring .15 decimals of land to the plaintiff by registered deeds dated 19.03.1980 and 21.03:1980 and inducted him into possession of the suit land. But the S.A. Khatian in respect of the suit land, inadvertently, was not prepared in the name of Mobaswar Ali and the same was wrongly prepared in the names of Tobarak Ali, Jahur Ali, Golabi Bibi and Gol Bibi. The plaintiff had been possessing suit land since his purchase but the defendant No. 1 without having any right, title and interest, all on a sudden, forcibly dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land on 01.10.1988 and hence the suit. 

 3. The defendant No.1 contested case by filing written statement contending, inter-alia, that the suit land appertaining to S. A. Plot Nos. 838 and 839 measuring 3 powas, approximately measuring 24 decimals of land 'lying within’ a compact block', originally belonged to one Ambor Ali who died leaving Sekendar Ali as son and Gol Bibi and Golabi Bibi as daughters and by amicable partition amongst them Sekendar Ali got the land now recorded in suit Plot No. 839 and his sisters in suit plot No. 838. Sekendar Ali transferred his entire share of the said parcel of land, now recorded 'in plot. No. 839 to the grand father of this defendant No. 1 whose heirs are in possession thereof 0.12 acres of land was recorded in plot No. 838 in the names of Gol Bibi and Golabi Bibi under S.A. Khatian No. 199 but the name of Tobarak Ali who had no interest in the land was wrongly recorded therein along with Golabi Bibi transferred the suit land to the defendant No. 1 vide two registered kabalas dated 03.12.1984 and. inducted him into possession thereof. The defendant No. 1 has been possessing the said land since then by erecting huts thereon. The plaintiff never had any right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and that the defendant No. 1 never dispossessed him from the suit land as alleged by the plaintiff and that the plaintiff hatched up this suit with false and baseless allegations with intent to grab the suit land and hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
